name: Secret RF

lead: Secret RF is a fractional radiofrequency microneedling device from Cutera, used in clinics for better skin quality and fewer facial wrinkles.

Fine needles enter the skin and deliver RF energy in a fractional pattern, which stimulates collagen remodeling as the skin heals. Two trials were registered in 2018; results are not summarized in the available sources.

paras: Treatment is done in a clinic by a trained provider. Results develop gradually over weeks as the skin remodels, and people commonly add a series of sessions or pair it with a standard skincare routine.

Expected effects are redness and swelling for a few days. Infection is a general microneedling risk when infection control is poor. Device-specific safety data are not covered in the available sources.

angle.text: Secret RF is used for better skin quality and fewer facial wrinkles. Microneedles deliver radiofrequency energy in a fractional pattern, which prompts collagen remodeling as the skin heals. Two registered studies exist.

lead: Secret RF is a fractional microneedling radiofrequency device made by Cutera and used in aesthetic medicine to improve skin quality and reduce facial wrinkles. A clinician passes a handpiece with fine needles over the face; people seek it for smoother texture, firmer-looking skin and softer lines.[1][2]

Microneedling in general is a cosmetic procedure in which tiny sterile needles puncture the skin repeatedly to prompt a healing response, and it has been used for scarring and acne with research ongoing; devices that add radiofrequency energy through the needles are a variant of the approach.[3]
Published information on Secret RF specifically is limited to two clinical trial registrations from 2018, one for skin quality and one for facial wrinkles.[1][2]
infobox: Skin quality, facial wrinkles (per registered studies)

paras: The device combines microneedling with radiofrequency energy, a category of in-clinic skin rejuvenation treatments. Microneedling procedures generally involve repeated skin punctures that prompt the body's repair response.[3]

The microneedling article reports that its main safety concern is infection risk when procedures are done in non-medical settings by people untrained in infection control, and notes an April 2024 CDC report of HIV diagnoses in three women after vampire facials at a New Mexico spa; that report concerned microneedling with platelet-rich plasma rather than RF devices.[3]

A multi-center clinical evaluation of the Cutera Secret RF device (27 participants, condition listed as skin quality) started in January 2018 and is listed as completed.[1] A separate 40-participant study of the Secret micro-needle fractional RF system for facial wrinkles started in February 2018; its status is listed as unknown.[2] Outcome results from these registrations were not found.

timeline.event: Two registered studies of Secret RF begin.[1][2]
